# The result of the product of two BallVectors: the radius, or NaN

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_conv_finish` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The result of the product of two BallVectors from its radius $r_z$, the mask $\mathit{okc}$ that every coefficient is finite and the mask $\mathit{okg}$ that the bound of the dot product was given: $r_z$ when both are true and $r_z$ is finite, with the flag $\mathit{flag}$ true; otherwise a NaN and the flag false, and the product is the whole space:

$$r = r_z \ \text{when } \mathit{okc} \text{ and } \mathit{okg} \text{ are true and } r_z \text{ is finite}, \qquad r = \mathrm{NaN} \text{ otherwise}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_conv_1`, called by `convolution`, the product of polynomials, of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_conv_2`, called by `convolution`, the product of polynomials, of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- $r_z$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $\mathit{okc}$ is a mask, true or false.
- $\mathit{okg}$ is a mask, true or false.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{flag}$ is true exactly when $\mathit{okc}$ and $\mathit{okg}$ are true and $r_z$ is finite.
- When it is, $r = r_z$.
- Otherwise $r$ is a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_conv_finish_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBvConv.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBvConv.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_conv_finish_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bv_conv_finish_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the finish of the product of polynomials of BallVector: the radius or the canonical NaN (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_conv_finish.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_conv_finish.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`norm_finish_1`](norm_finish_1.md).

```
# The finish of the product of two BallVectors (milestone2.md, "The product of polynomials": bv_conv_k):
# the radius of conv_radius, with the flag true, when every coefficient written is finite (okc, the
# mask of the convolution conv_k of the centers), the bound of dot for min(n_x, n_y) terms was given
# (okg, the mask of bound_dot_k) and the radius is finite; otherwise the canonical NaN and the flag
# false, and the product is the whole space. norm_finish_1 under the and of the two masks. Proposed in
# experiments/milestone2/kernels/ and checked there by bv_conv.py, with this listing.

q         = and(okc, okg)
(r, flag) = norm_finish_1(rz, q)
```
